messages:
jon: Quick heads-up — brought up the compact ranking model (v2-compact) on the eval harness with the new fused-kernel runtime + int4. Overall tokens/cost look good but saw a ~-2.7% NDCG@10 on the benchmark. MRR almost unchanged. Any quick suspects?

priya: how are you scoring? same golds + candidate pool as previous runs? :thinking_face:

jon: same golds and candidate pool A. I re-used the snapshot from last week. harness run id: `run/2026-03-21-01` (link: https://ci.internal/runs/2026-03-21-01)

alex: can you paste the eval config you used? especially any new preprocess or candidate-normalization flags.

jon: sure — config snippet:```json
{"tokenizer":"hf/sentencepiece-v3","candidate_normalizer":"strip_html_keep_punct","batch_size":16,"kernel":"fused_attn_v3"}
```

micaela: hmm. `strip_html_keep_punct` wasn't used in the last golden run, right? last one was `strip_html_strip_punct`. That can affect short snippets. Also fused_attn_v3 changed KV layout in cache — if batch_size moved from 8->16 ordering jitter can happen.

sam: quick check: slice metrics by query length? I suspect short queries losing signal. run a per-slice NDCG/MRR.

jon: did that — paste results:```
len<=5: ndcg10 -5.1%, mrr -0.4%
6-15: ndcg10 -1.3%, mrr +0.1%
>15: ndcg10 +0.2%, mrr +0.3%
```

priya: yep short queries are the hit. Could be candidate formatting or a subtle tokenization shift with the new SP model. Did the tokenizer artifact change? any vocabulary drift?

alex: also check candidate dedupe ordering. We had a bug where dedupe used stable hash that depended on in-memory order; increased batch sizes changed in-flight ordering and the final ranked pool differed slightly. Small diffs can drop NDCG more than MRR.

jon: good point — I re-ran with `batch_size=8` and `candidate_normalizer=strip_html_strip_punct` and kept fused kernel. New run `run/2026-03-21-02` metrics:```
overall ndcg10 -0.6%, mrr +0.0%
len<=5: ndcg10 -1.2%
```

micaela: that suggests two contributors: normalization + batch-ordering. For the cache layout / fused kernel interaction we should also try `fused_attn_v2` (older kernel) — the new one optimizes for throughput but reorders some ops.

ci-bot: CI: eval/run/2026-03-21-03 queued — tests: per-slice NDCG/MRR, candidate-order-diff, tokenizer-diff.

sam: another quick idea — run with canonicalized candidate texts (lowercase, whitespace-collapse) to isolate punctuation/tokenizer deltas. small script: `scripts/normalize_candidates.sh --lower --collapse-ws`

jon: ran that with batch=8 + fused_attn_v3 + strip_html_strip_punct. run/2026-03-21-03 results:```
overall ndcg10 +0.1%, mrr +0.2%
len<=5: ndcg10 -0.3%
len<=5 top1 precision +0.5%
```

priya: interesting — normalization recovered a lot. suggests the model is sensitive to punctuation anchoring in short queries. For onboarding checklist: add candidate canonicalization step and a per-length smoke check.

alex: action items: 1) run kernel A (fused_attn_v2) vs kernel B (v3) with same batch=8 and canonicalized candidates, 2) add a tokenizer parity test between SP-v2 and SP-v3, 3) add candidate-order stabilizer in eval harness. I'll file a quick ticket.

micaela: +1. I'll own the kernel comparison. I'm curious if TPU kernel fallback had any numeric scaling differences around softmax temps. I'll diff logits for a small seed set.

jon: thanks all — I'll update the onboarding doc with the normalization step and re-run the full benchmark with kernel A/B and post results tomorrow morning. :coffee:

sam: nice triage. If we get consistent recovery we can proceed with v2-compact onboard. If not, we'll escalate to model team for a small recalibration pass.

jon: updated — leaving the run links in the ticket. cc @priya @micaela
